To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interactions between metals and their correlations with biological parameters in the placenta and fetal membrane are more complex than previously reported, and that the correlations with the biological parameters in the umbilical are similar to those in the placenta.

the concentrations of the elements in the placenta and afterbirths were significantly correlated with maternal age, gestation age, placental and newborn parameters and that the interactions between the elements in these tissues may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of pregnancy and newborn diseases.

14 elements were determined in 100 placenta, 100 fetal membrane and 100 umbilical cord; interactions between the elements were observed; relationships between the elements and biological parameters (maternal age, gestational and newborn parameters, placenta parameters) were found
In summary, our research is concerned with
interactions between the concentrations of 14 elements in the human placenta, fetal membranes and umbilical cords
the relationships between the concentrations and interactions between the elements in the afterbir
the relationships between the concentration of macroelements, microelements and heavy metals in the placenta and fetal membrane
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactions between metal elements in placental tissues and the biological parameters are very important for the development of the fetus and newborn.

the relationships observed in the present study are the result of the influence of the placenta, fetus and newborn on the metal elements in the placenta and fetal membrane, as well as the influence of the mother’s age and pregnancy on the metal elements of the placenta and umbilical cords.
the placenta, the umbilical blood and the umbilical vein are not a barrier to metal elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the placenta, the fetal membrane and the umbilical cords should be considered as a whole, and the results of the analysis of these tissues are important for the assessment of the health status of the mother and newborn.
the relationships between metals and the afterbirth parameters are complex and depend on the element, tissue and parameter.
the concentrations of metals in the placenta are influenced by the concentrations of metals from the maternal blood.
